policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'came to Ephesus' renders either the simple or the compounded verb of arrival; nothing in the English or its notes distinguishes them, so the base fallback carries the projection.

ASV coordinates the two verbs of the sentence ('came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples') while rendering the preceding participle as a participle ('having passed through the upper country'). The parallel finite 'found' answers the infinitive alongside the infinitive of arrival, not the participial reading, which ASV's own practice in this verse would have shown as 'and having found'.
The connective is at most the 'and' opening 'and he said unto them', which ASV supplies routinely between clauses whether or not the particle stands; nothing distinguishes its presence.

ASV 'And they said unto him' requires a verb of speaking in English on either reading, since the shorter text leaves it to be understood from the preceding clause; the wording does not show whether the verb stood in the Greek. The verse's only note is an alternative rendering of 'was a Holy Spirit' and does not touch this unit.

ASV reads simply 'And he said, Into what then were ye baptized?' with no indirect object; the longer reading's 'unto them' is unrepresented, and ASV renders that phrase explicitly wherever it stands (as in v. 2, 'he said unto them').
The added particle is a correlative with no separate English exponent; ASV 'John baptized with the baptism of repentance' is the same on either reading.
ASV ends the verse 'that is, on Jesus', with the single name; the longer reading's added title would give 'on Christ Jesus', and ASV translates that title wherever it stands.
The variant is the article before 'hands', which ASV renders as the possessive 'his hands' on either reading; the English shows nothing.
Both readings are spellings of the numeral twelve and yield ASV 'about twelve men' alike.

ASV 'persuading as to the things concerning the kingdom of God' has an explicit substantival 'the things', which answers the neuter article of the longer reading; the shorter reading gives only 'persuading concerning the kingdom of God'.

ASV reads 'in the school of Tyrannus' with no indefinite qualifier; the longer reading's 'a certain' would appear, as ASV supplies it elsewhere in the chapter ('a certain man named Demetrius', v. 24).
ASV reads 'heard the word of the Lord', without the added name that the longer reading would give as 'the word of the Lord Jesus' — a phrase ASV does print in full at v. 17 where the name stands.
The variant is the order of subject and verb, which English fixes as 'God wrought' either way; the note on this verse is a Greek gloss on 'miracles' and touches nothing here.

ASV 'were carried away from his body' renders the verb compounded with 'away from', matching the following 'from his body'; the competing compound means to bring upon and would not yield 'carried away'.
ASV ends 'and the evil spirits went out', with no 'from them'; the competing reading adds that prepositional phrase, which ASV represents wherever it stands.

ASV 'But certain also of the strolling Jews' has the adverbial 'also', which renders the conjunction of the base reading; the competing reading substitutes a preposition and leaves nothing for 'also' to translate.
ASV 'I adjure you by Jesus' is first person singular; the competing reading is first person plural and would give 'we adjure'.
The variant adds an article inside 'Jesus whom Paul preacheth'; the relative clause is identical in English on either reading.
ASV 'seven sons of one Sceva' attaches the indefinite to the name, as the base reading does; the competing reading attaches it to 'sons' ('certain sons of Sceva'), which ASV does not read.

ASV places 'sons' with the numeral, 'there were seven sons of one Sceva', which is the base reading's word; the competing reading has already supplied 'sons' earlier (excluded at v019) and leaves only an article here, so the English requires the base word at this point. 'Who did this' renders the following participle either way.
ASV 'the evil spirit answered and said unto them' has the indirect object the competing reading omits. The verse's note is an alternative rendering of 'know' and does not touch this unit.
The variant adds a correlative particle answered by the following conjunction; ASV 'Jesus I know, and Paul I know' is the same on either reading.
Both readings are forms of the same verb of leaping, differing in tense stem alone; ASV 'leaped on them' does not distinguish them.
The variant is the order of subject and prepositional phrase; English fixes it as 'the man ... leaped on them' either way.
ASV 'and mastered both of them' has 'both', the base reading's word; the competing reading has a plain pronoun ('mastered them') and adds a conjunction, neither of which accounts for 'both'.
Simple and compounded forms of the same verb; ASV 'fear fell upon them all' renders either, the 'upon' coming from the following preposition.
The variant is word order within the same phrase; ASV 'the word of the Lord' is identical on either reading.
Both readings are forms of the city's name and are rendered 'Jerusalem' alike.
The variant is the order of the noun and its negated modifier; ASV 'brought no little business' is the same on either reading.

ASV recasts the clause as 'by this business we have our wealth', which supplies both a subject 'we' and a possessive 'our'; that paraphrase fits the dative of advantage and the possessive genitive equally.
The variant is the order of 'temple' and the goddess's name; ASV 'the temple of the great goddess Diana' fixes English order either way, and the note here is only a Greek gloss on the name.
Two connective particles with the same force in this clause; ASV 'and that she should even be deposed' renders either.

ASV makes the goddess the subject and her magnificence the thing she is deposed from: 'she should even be deposed from her magnificence'. That is the base reading's genitive of separation; the competing accusative makes 'her magnificence' the thing destroyed, which ASV would render 'her magnificence should be destroyed'.
ASV 'And the city was filled with the confusion' lacks 'whole', which the longer reading adds and which ASV renders wherever it stands.
The variant is the position of the connective and the presence of an article with the name; ASV 'And when Paul was minded' shows neither.

ASV's text, 'they brought Alexander out of the multitude', suits both verbs — the one meaning to bring together or instruct and the one meaning to bring forward. The verse's only note is classed an alternative rendering ('Or, And some of the multitude instructed Alexander') and so cannot decide the reading.
Both readings are particles of approximation rendered 'about the space of two hours' alike.
The variant is the order of subject and object; ASV 'when the townclerk had quieted the multitude' fixes English order either way.
ASV 'what man is there who knoweth not' renders the nominative singular directly and the partitive genitive plural idiomatically alike; the English does not show which stood.
ASV reads 'temple-keeper of the great Diana' without 'goddess', which the longer reading adds; ASV prints that word where it stands, as at v. 27, 'the great goddess Diana'.
ASV 'blasphemers of our goddess' is first person; the competing reading is second person and would give 'your goddess'.

ASV 'if ye seek anything about other matters' has a preposition and a plural 'other matters', which is the competing reading's two words; the base reading is a single comparative adverb meaning 'further' and would give 'anything further'.
Simple and compounded forms of the verb 'give'; ASV 'give account' renders either. The verse's note is an alternative rendering of the clause about the day's riot and does not touch this unit.
ASV 'give account of this concourse' uses 'of', which serves the prepositional reading and the bare genitive of the omitting reading alike.
